query:
In the discussion of mono pressings versus fold-down stereo cuts, one member argues that listening will show you the difference even where measurements look clean. Who actually made that argument?

Options:
A. Bram
B. Marcy
C. Theo
D. Felix
context:
[1] (about=Theo, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:14:00) Bram is right. I would add: even where measurements are clean, the sound character of a mono cut still differs in ways the measurements undersell. in my view this is one place where listening leads.
[2] (about=Bram, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:11:00) good question Dev, both. mono uses a horizontal-only cutting head and a dedicated mono tape if one exists, fold-down is a stereo cut summed to mono playback. they sound different. the mono cut is louder and more present, the fold-down is just half a stereo. listening tests will show you, even without measurements.
[3] (about=Dev, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:08:00) lowkey question, what is the actual difference between a mono pressing and a fold-down stereo? I keep reading conflicting stuff and ngl I'm getting confused. is it the cutting head or the master tape or both??
[4] (about=Ines, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:58:00) Maeve facts 💖 saw a Heart cassette get sold at the market last week with louder cut than the LP. someone is doing god's work somewhere
[5] (about=Lina, episodic, t8 @2026-02-09T19:27:00) Dev, I have changed on this. I had a hearing test last week. The audiologist suggested some mid-range compensation. I have started doing focused, louder sessions in the evening. Beethoven 9 last night at concert level, alone with the Quad ESLs. It was different.
[6] (about=Maeve, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:30:00) okay personal news, my grandmother passed last month and I inherited her console stereo!!! a 1962 Magnavox astro-sonic, it is gigantic and gorgeous. I have moved my primary listening from the studio nearfields to the console. it is a different relationship to listening, the speakers are integral, the cabinet is the room, and grandma is in the wood. I'm not going back.
[7] (about=Marcy, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:05:00) fwiw the Blue Note monos from that era have a specific kind of cut that cleans up beautifully if you have the gear. happy to A/B them at the studio if Sander brings them by, just my read on what they're worth before anyone sells.
[8] (about=Olin, episodic, t12 @2026-02-23T19:43:00) On the streaming question; one. Workshop and home listening serve different functions. Two. Lossless streaming has closed most of the gap on the technical side. Three. The remaining gap is ritual and ownership, not sound. Four. We should stop fighting about format and fight about mastering.
[9] (about=Quint, episodic, t12 @2026-02-23T19:02:00) okay something I never thought Id say out loud. my daughter set up tidal on the shop laptop christmas time. I was going to ignore it and my hands have been busy on a cabinet. and now I find myself listening to it 4 hours at a stretch in the workshop. its convenient. at home I still play vinyl exclusively but at the shop tidal is what I'm doing. youngsters were right about convenience, the music is the same.
[10] (about=Sander, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T18:53:00) mostly straight ahead jazz, a few Blue Note original mono pressings if I'm reading the labels right. the family had no idea what they had. they wanted it gone.
[11] (about=Yuko, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:20:00) A measurement-based view: well-mastered hi-res digital at 24/96 is indistinguishable from a clean LP at the threshold of human hearing for most listeners. The remaining differences are in mastering and pressing variance. Hema's shift is technically sound.
